बॉलीवु़ड के गलियारों से आया है एक एकदम मसालेदार किस्सा! 🍿
राणा डग्गुबाती ने हाल ही में मुंबई के मेहबूब स्टूडियोज में IFP 2026 के दौरान एक मजेदार खुलासा किया है। 🎬
उन्होंने बताया कि 2013 में रिलीज हुई फिल्म Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani में उनका कैमियो बिल्कुल अचानक हुआ था। 🤩
राणा का दावा है कि पहले यह रोल कोई दूसरा बड़ा स्टार करने वाला था, लेकिन उसके मना करने पर रणबीर और डायरेक्टर अयान मुखर्जी उनके होटल के कमरे में पहुंच गए। ✈️
वे दोनों उन्हें एक तरह से किडनैप करके रात में ही उदयपुर फ्लाइट से ले गए, जहां उन्होंने शूटिंग की और सुबह वापस अपने सेट पर लौट आए। 📸
इस फिल्म में राणा ने विक्रम जायसवाल नाम के फोटोग्राफर का किरदार निभाया था, जो अदिति की शादी में नैना यानी दीपिका पादुकोण से फ्लर्ट करता है। 💑
अदिति का किरदार कल्कि कोचलिन ने निभाया था, और फिल्म को करण जौहर तथा हीरू यश जौहर के बैनर धर्मा प्रोडक्शंस के तहत बनाया गया था। ✨
क्या आपको Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani फिल्म में राणा डग्गुबाती का यह छोटा सा कैमियो सीन याद है? नीचे कमेंट्स में बताओ! 👇

ctx.title: Rana Daggubati recalls Ranbir Kapoor, Ayan Mukerji ‘kidnapping’ him for Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani cameo while he was shooting another film
ctx.summary: Rana Daggubati said he remembers little about his Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani cameo, which he filmed overnight in Udaipur.
ctx.text:
Rana Daggubati made a brief cameo in Ranbir Kapoor and Deepika Padukone -starrer Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani, which was released in 2013. Recently, while speaking at IFP 2026 (India Film Project) at Mehboob Studios in Mumbai, Rana recalled how Ranbir and the film’s director, Ayan Mukerji, unexpectedly roped him in for the cameo.
Recalling the incident, Rana shared that another big star was initially supposed to play the role but declined the offer. Ayan and Ranbir then approached him. The duo persuaded him to travel with them to Udaipur for the cameo while he was shooting for another project.
He said, "I am friends with Ranbir and Ayan. Some big star was supposed to play that, and that star said no. So these guys came to my hotel room where I was staying and shooting for some other film. They just kidnapped me and said you have to come to Udaipur tonight with us. They took me on the flight and shot that scene with me and came back."
Rana also spoke about how he approaches cameo roles, saying he does not think of them in the same way as full-fledged parts. He added, “That’s as much as I can remember about cameos. So, I vaguely remember something happened in the night. I shot something and I was back in the morning to another set. So I was like, something has happened. That's as much as I remember about the cameo."
In Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani, Rana played Vikram Jaiswal, a photographer who is shooting at Aditi’s (Kalki Koechlin) wedding. Aditi is a close friend of Naina (Deepika Padukone) and Bunny (Ranbir Kapoor). During the cameo, Vikram tries to flirt with Naina, prompting Bunny to step in and pull him away. The interaction leads to a confrontation between the two men.
Directed by Ayan Mukerji and produced by Karan Johar and Hiroo Yash Johar under the banner of Dharma Productions, Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani was released in theatres in , 2013. The romantic comedy followed four friends whose lives and relationships evolve as they reunite at different stages of their lives. The film became a major box-office success and remains popular among the audience,especially for its music.
Meanwhile, Ranbir is geraing up for the release of his next film Ramayana, which is set to release on November 5. Deepika, on the other hand, will be seen in Shah Rukh Khan's King and Allu Arjun's Raaka.
Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows.

Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today.

At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through film reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, celebrity interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing.
